identification.why: A claim is not enough and a fingerprint is not enough. The variable states the intent; the fingerprint refuses the claim when the hardware contradicts it. Neither present means no machine, which means the run skips.

display.why: Criterion 30 gates a missed-frame fraction at whatever interval the display reports. The same millisecond figure is a different claim on a different panel: 4.2 ms is the whole budget here and a quarter of it at 60 Hz.

electronResidentMb.why: The consent copy said about 30 MB. The floor with a live window and zero textures is 307 MB; the string had to change.
electronResidentMb.staleBecause: Measured on Electron 33 with WebGL textures simulating the shelf. The product ships Electron 44 and phase 1 renders DOM only, so these are estimates until re-probed. They are recorded rather than removed because the argument they settled — that the consent copy was false by an order of magnitude — does not depend on the exact figure.

hotkeyToVisibleMs.why: Residency is a 30-minute hybrid: 9 ms when a press matters, 232 MB when it does not.

scrollFramePacing.driver: injected wheel events through the real compositor path, never by assigning scrollTop
scrollFramePacing.why: This measurement is why phase 1 ships DOM only — no canvas, no WebGL, no texture atlas.

machines.measuredReason: Nothing has been run on Reference B. Its budgets are budgets. A figure printed for B that came from an A run would be the same error as reporting an extrapolation as a measurement, and B is also where criterion 29's untestable Linux GPU behaviour lives.
